main_concerns.concern: The main AI is treating gap-closure evidence as sufficient to close the active RedCap revival goal, even though the committed lifecycle state and the E2E's own Prism self-check both signal that the system is only temporarily usable, not formally ready for engineering work. The failure backlog closed two real issues (browser automation unavailable, Prism full self-check failure) as 'non-blocking' rather than resolving them, which conflicts with the user's instruction to run repeated E2E loops until no issues or omissions remain.

The evidence chain is structurally self-referential: Prism audit reviewed Prism, prism-resolution passed its own resolution, and now Prism re-reviews Prism's prior review. Each layer validates the previous without external ground truth. The dedicated receipts (forge, arsenal, project-install) address the form of the prior block ("no dedicated evidence") but their content is unverifiable — receipt JSON files can be generated without actual tool execution. Combined with a dirty git baseline, the closure claim rests on evidence that validates itself.

minimum_fixes.minimum_fix: Before marking the active goal complete, either (a) fix the RedCap package-level Prism self-check failures and any remaining lifecycle blockers, then run one more E2E loop that passes without non-blocking closures, or (b) obtain explicit user sign-off that TEMPORARY_USABLE plus the documented non-blocking failures satisfies 'formally used for engineering work'. Do not close the goal solely on gap-closure receipts and a single round2 E2E.

Commit the uncommitted task-health.json and task-ledger.jsonl changes (or stash/discard them with an explicit decision record), then re-verify the baseline at a new commit SHA before claiming closure. Additionally, add at least one non-Prism verification step — e.g., a direct shell invocation of `runtime/bin/redcap forge --self-check` with captured output — to break the self-referential review chain for the most critical claim.
